title: W(2,5) = 178
statement: The van der Waerden number W(2,5) is exactly 178: every 2-colouring of {1,...,178} contains an arithmetic progression of length 5 monochromatic in colour 1; or an arithmetic progression of length 5 monochromatic in colour 2; and some 2-colouring of {1,...,177} contains none of them.

concept_refs.note: van der Waerden numbers are the arithmetic-progression case of the Ramsey-type colouring problems

provenance.conjectured_by: Not a conjecture: every value here is a published exact number, reproduced from both sides as a gate on the encoder. The contribution is the machine-checked refutation, not the number.
searched_by: axeyum proof-producing CDCL core (solve_with_drat_proof / solve_with_drat_proof_streaming, pure Rust, ADR-0381), both sides
checked_by: axeyum in-tree backward DRAT checker (check_drat_backward, ADR-0382, pure Rust)

VanDerWaerden::first_violation -- a dynamic program over pairs of members of the colour class, computing the longest progression, which shares no code with the encoder's (first term, common difference) enumeration -- replayed the witness
scripts/check-claim-certificates.py: a third derivation of the semantics, in Python, independent of both the Rust encoder and the Rust verifier

prior_art.citation: R. S. Stevens and R. Shantaram, Computer-generated van der Waerden partitions, Mathematics of Computation 32 (1978), 635-636

evidence.supports: the formula both other rows are about is W(2,5) at n=178
evidence.notes: The deciding instance itself. check-claim-certificates.py validates it clause by clause against an independent Python derivation of the semantics -- every negative clause a genuine progression of the length its colour carries, the structural clauses exactly the sound at-least-one / at-most-one / symmetry set for this instance's block structure, and the per-colour clause counts equal to the progression counts -- so the refutation beside it provably refutes this instance and not some other file.

Found by the CDCL core, then replayed by VanDerWaerden::first_violation (independent of the encoder) before being written, and replayed a third time in Python by check-claim-certificates.py, which grows progressions forward from every pair of same-coloured points.

Produced by axeyum's own proof-producing CDCL core (solve_with_drat_proof_streaming, ADR-0381) streaming TEXT DRAT to disk, and re-derived in the same process by axeyum's own backward DRAT checker (check_drat_backward, ADR-0382). No external solver and no external checker took part. The deciding CNF beside it is validated clause by clause by check-claim-certificates.py against an independent Python derivation of the semantics, including the clause COUNT per colour: this family has no subsumption reduction (every length-k progression has exactly k points, so no two nest), so the encoding must carry every progression.

notes: REPRODUCES a published value; the contribution is the certification, not the number. As far as an audit of the literature reached (Ahmed-Kullmann-Snevily arXiv:1102.5433, OEIS A007783 and A005346, and a GitHub survey), no classical van der Waerden number carries a machine-checked UNSAT proof in the peer-reviewed record: AKS say explicitly that compressing their resolution proofs into a checkable object 'would be highly desirable', and Marijn Heule's vdWaerden repository holds only lower-bound colourings. Both sides are discharged here -- n = N-1 satisfiable with an independently replayed colouring, n = N refuted with a DRAT proof re-derived by axeyum's own checker, no external solver or checker anywhere (ADR-0002). SOUNDNESS NOTE on symmetry: colour classes may be ordered by least element only between colours forbidding the SAME progression length. Diagonal instances take the uniform whole-palette break, which is sound because their colours are interchangeable; off-diagonal instances get per-length blocks, which for w(2;3,t) with t != 3 means NO colour symmetry at all. crates/axeyum-search/tests/vdw.rs carries the negative control showing the whole-palette break turning satisfiable w(2;3,4) at n=17 into unsat.
